questions.subject: Social and Citizenship Studies
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish good and poor leadership qualities using reasons from a school-group situation.
questions.prompt: Two group leaders allocate coloured paper. One asks what each pupil needs and shares it fairly; the other keeps the best pieces for friends. Name a leadership quality shown by each and explain the difference.
questions.answer: The first shows fairness and consideration; the second shows favouritism. One considers the whole group, while the other gives friends an unfair advantage.
questions.explanation: The judgement rests on described choices, not popularity.

markingGuide.description: Identifies fairness/consideration in the first action.
Identifies favouritism and explains the unequal treatment.

questions.subject: Social and Citizenship Studies
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish good and poor leadership qualities using reasons from a school-group situation.
questions.prompt: A team leader’s first arrangement fails. The leader admits the mistake and invites another suggestion. Explain two good leadership qualities shown.

markingGuide.description: Explains honesty/accountability from the admission.

questions.learningObjective: Explain a benefit of good leadership and connect it to a group outcome.
questions.prompt: Before a class display is assembled, its leader explains the goal and checks that everyone understands their part. Describe one likely benefit and how the leader’s action produces it.

questions.subject: Social and Citizenship Studies
questions.learningObjective: Demonstrate fair, cooperative leadership during an actually observed small-group task.
questions.prompt: Lead an actual small group in arranging reusable paper shapes into a display on a desk. Ask for ideas, agree fair roles and check the group’s progress. The examiner must observe your own leadership; do not submit a written plan instead.

questions.learningObjective: Explain responsible followership as thoughtful cooperation in a shared task.

questions.subject: Social and Citizenship Studies
questions.learningObjective: Explain tolerance, inclusion and respect as related but different ideas.
questions.prompt: Explain the difference between tolerance, inclusion and respect using a family discussion as your example.
questions.answer: Tolerance allows people to have different views without hostility. Inclusion gives each person a chance to take part. Respect means treating each person with consideration and listening politely.
questions.explanation: Tolerance does not require agreement with every idea or acceptance of harm.

markingGuide.description: Explains tolerance of differing views.

Explains respect as considerate treatment.

questions.learningObjective: Describe ways of showing tolerance, inclusion and respect in a fictional family situation.
questions.prompt: Two members of a fictional household prefer different activities for a shared free period. Suggest a respectful way to agree a plan without insisting that one person always gives way.
questions.answer: Listen to both preferences and agree a fair arrangement, such as taking turns or choosing an activity both accept.
questions.explanation: Accept different feasible solutions supported by respect and inclusion.

markingGuide.description: Includes listening to both people.
Proposes a fair workable arrangement rather than permanent one-sided surrender.

questions.subject: Social and Citizenship Studies
questions.learningObjective: Demonstrate respectful listening and inclusion during an actually observed fictional family-meeting role.
questions.prompt: In an actual supervised role activity, take part in a fictional family meeting to choose a game. Invite a quieter member’s idea, listen without interruption and respond respectfully to a different preference. Use fictional roles only; do not discuss your own household.
questions.answer: Observed evidence includes an invitation to contribute, actual listening and a respectful response that allows differing preferences.
questions.explanation: This assesses individual demonstrated conduct in a simulation, not the quality of the learner’s real family relationships. No performance has occurred during authoring.

markingGuide.description: Actually invites another member to contribute.
Actually listens without interrupting.
Responds respectfully to a differing preference.

questions.subject: Social and Citizenship Studies
questions.topic: Effects of Family/personal values and norms on relationships
questions.learningObjective: Identify personal and family values or norms that can influence relationships.
questions.prompt: A fictional household agrees to tell one another before borrowing possessions. One member also personally values being punctual. Identify the family norm and the personal value, and explain the difference.
questions.answer: The shared borrowing agreement is the family norm. Punctuality is the stated personal value. A shared expectation and a person’s guiding principle can both affect relationships.
questions.explanation: A value and a norm can be related; this supplied example is not a universal family rule.

markingGuide.description: Identifies the shared borrowing norm.
Identifies punctuality and distinguishes personal from shared guidance.

questions.subject: Social and Citizenship Studies
questions.topic: Effects of Family/personal values and norms on relationships
questions.learningObjective: Explain effects of selected personal or family norms on relationships.
questions.prompt: Two fictional households follow different visiting customs. In one, visitors arrange a time; in the other, familiar visitors often arrive without notice. Explain how an unspoken difference could lead to misunderstanding and how to reduce it.
questions.answer: An unexpected visit might seem inconsiderate to one household while seeming ordinary to the other. Explaining preferences and agreeing a suitable time can reduce misunderstanding.
questions.explanation: No custom is labelled universally superior; the example assesses effects on relationships.

markingGuide.description: Explains the different interpretation caused by the norm.
Suggests respectful communication or agreement.

questions.subject: Social and Citizenship Studies
questions.topic: Effects of Family/personal values and norms on relationships
questions.learningObjective: Explain effects of selected personal or family norms on relationships.
questions.prompt: A person promises to return a cousin’s drawing but delays repeatedly without an explanation. Explain how the personal habit affects the relationship, even if the drawing is eventually returned.
questions.answer: Repeated unexplained delay can weaken trust because the cousin cannot rely on the promise. Returning it later does not by itself remove the uncertainty created.
questions.explanation: The focus is the relational effect of a habit, rather than ownership or a legal claim.

markingGuide.description: Explains weakened trust or reliability.
Links the effect to repeated unexplained delay despite eventual return.

questions.subject: Social and Citizenship Studies
questions.topic: Effects of Family/personal values and norms on relationships
questions.learningObjective: Identify religious or cultural values and norms in a supplied fictional description without generalising to every community.
questions.prompt: Read this fictional account: “In this family’s tradition, guests are welcomed with a greeting. During a religious gathering, members keep a quiet period for reflection.” Identify one cultural norm and one religious norm in the supplied account.
questions.answer: Welcoming guests with the customary greeting is the cultural norm described. Keeping the quiet reflection period at the religious gathering is the religious norm described.
questions.explanation: These are fictional descriptions; they are not claims about every family, culture or religion.

markingGuide.description: Identifies the greeting as the supplied cultural norm.
Identifies quiet reflection as the supplied religious norm.

questions.subject: Social and Citizenship Studies
questions.topic: Effects of Family/personal values and norms on relationships
questions.learningObjective: Explain how differing religious or cultural norms can affect a relationship and how respectful communication can help.
questions.prompt: A visitor talks during the quiet reflection period described in a fictional religious gathering because the custom was not explained. Describe a respectful response and how it could protect the relationship.
questions.answer: Explain the quiet period kindly and help the visitor understand what is expected, without mocking them. Clear, considerate communication can prevent an unfamiliar custom from becoming a personal conflict.
questions.explanation: Learning a custom does not require a person to adopt another religion or disclose their beliefs.

markingGuide.description: Proposes kind explanation without humiliation.
Connects understanding the norm with avoiding conflict or protecting trust.

questions.subject: Social and Citizenship Studies
questions.learningObjective: Explain selected differences and similarities in supplied fictional beliefs or traditions without stereotyping.
questions.prompt: Two fictional communities use different greetings for guests but both intend to make guests welcome. Explain one difference and one similarity in their traditions without claiming that every member acts identically.
questions.answer: The form of greeting differs. The shared purpose is welcoming guests. The description does not establish that every person always follows the custom.
questions.explanation: Supplied fictional evidence supports comparison without ranking cultures.

markingGuide.description: Identifies the different form of greeting.
Identifies the shared welcoming purpose without a universal stereotype.

questions.subject: Social and Citizenship Studies
questions.learningObjective: Explain how understanding cultural differences can promote fairness, unity and good neighbourliness.
questions.prompt: A pupil learns that a neighbour’s unfamiliar celebration is important to that neighbour. Explain how understanding this difference could support good neighbourliness, even if the pupil does not join the celebration.
questions.answer: Understanding can encourage considerate questions and respectful treatment instead of ridicule. Neighbours can remain friendly and fair while observing different traditions.
questions.explanation: No actual attendance, religious practice or disclosure is assigned.

markingGuide.description: Connects understanding with a concrete respectful response.
Explains friendly/fair relations without requiring identical participation.

questions.learningObjective: Explain selected national values using concrete examples.
questions.prompt: Give an actual short spoken explanation to an examiner of one national value from this lesson and an original everyday example that shows it. Explain why the example fits. A written script alone is not the response.
questions.answer: A possible heard response explains cooperation and describes classmates sharing ideas to finish a common display, then connects their joint effort to the value. Other accurate values and examples are acceptable.
